title: Runtime identity lock requirements v1
description: What the pinned patch series must keep carrying for a task to stay bound to the code it was admitted under. Each requirement is anchored to one line a named patch adds, because a check that parsed the TypeScript would be a second reading of a source the manifest already pins byte for byte.

id.description: Named so the contract can explain it and the validator can require that it does.

requires.description: What must hold, said as a property rather than as a line of code.

why.description: What goes wrong when it stops holding. A requirement whose cost nobody can state is one nobody will defend.

patch.description: The patch file, as the manifest names it. The manifest pins its bytes, and this check verifies that pin before reading the line.

added_line.description: One line the patch adds, verbatim and without its `+`. Anchoring to a line the patch adds means the requirement is met by bytes under the manifest's digest rather than by a pattern that happens to match.

occurrences.description: How many times that patch adds exactly this line. A count rather than a presence test: a line that appears twice where one was expected is a copy someone made, and the requirement stops describing what it checks.

lock_digest.description: sha256 over this document with the field removed, so the requirement set is bound as a set.
